![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14253560/assets/75b3a8b6aa11ac54edd5e3f0d694514cf7e63eefd05313ab854ddd917aa32ad5.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{1}{4},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta .$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14253560/assets/73972bbedd114db6635eaec98dd0989f7d6e877aa276b381973b753204e2b8e8.png)

We're given that $x=\frac{1}{4}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{4}.$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{4}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{1}{4})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{1}{16}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{15}{16}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we select the negative answer since $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ is negative in the fourth quadrant. So $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =-\frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}.$

Finally, knowing that $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{(-\frac{\sqrt{15}}{4})}=-\frac{4}{\sqrt{15}}=-\frac{4\sqrt{15}}{15}.
$$
